bird:beer_factory: This database tracks root beer retail activity, cataloging root beer brands along with their breweries, ingredients, packaging options, social media presence, and pricing. The only people in it are the customers, stored with their contact details, addresses, first purchase dates, and email subscription status. The main transactional tables record individual root beer items sold (by brand, container type, selling location, and purchase date), the sales transactions in which customers buy those items at a particular store location with a credit card and price, and customer reviews that pair a customer with a brand they rated in stars and commented on.
bird:address: This database is a United States postal geography and demographics reference built around ZIP codes, with supporting lookups for states and core-based statistical areas. The only table of individual persons is congress, which lists members of the US House of Representatives with their names, party, state, House, and district; person-related numbers elsewhere, such as population, employees, and Social Security beneficiaries in zip_data, are aggregate counts rather than individuals. The main fact table is zip_data, which records per-ZIP-code statistics covering population by race, age and gender, households, income and home values, businesses, payroll, mailboxes, and monthly benefit payments, while mapping tables such as zip_congress, area_code, country, alias, and avoid link each ZIP code to congressional districts, telephone area codes, counties, and acceptable or unacceptable city names.
bird:book_publishing_company: This is a book publishing database (the classic pubs schema) that tracks publishers, the books (titles) they publish, the authors who write them, the stores that sell them, and the employees who work for the publishers. The people in it are authors, held in the authors table, and employees of the publishing houses, held in the employee table along with their jobs and job levels; stores act as the selling customers but are businesses rather than individuals. The main transactional table is sales, which records individual store orders of specific titles with quantities, dates, and payment terms, while titleauthor is the key fact/linking table connecting authors to the books they wrote with their order and royalty share, supported by roysched and discounts, which define royalty tiers and quantity-based store discounts.
bird:books: This database models an online bookstore, covering its book catalog, the people and companies behind the books, and the sales side of the business. The people in it are customers, stored in the customer table with names and emails, and authors, stored in the author table and linked to their titles through book_author, while supporting tables describe books, publishers, languages, countries, addresses, and shipping options. The main transactional tables are cust_order, which records each order a customer places along with its date, shipping method, and destination address; order_line, which records the individual books and prices within each order; and order_history, which tracks the changing status of each order over time, from receipt through delivery, cancellation, or return.
bird:car_retails: This database models a wholesale distributor of classic model cars (a classic order-management schema), tracking offices, staff, customers, product lines, individual products, and sales activity. The people appear in two tables: employees, who are assigned to offices and linked to one another through a reportsTo hierarchy, and customers, each of whom has a named contact and is assigned a sales representative from the employees table. The main transactional tables are orders, which records each sales order placed by a customer, orderdetails, which stores the line items of each order (product, quantity, and unit price), and payments, which captures customer check payments applied to their accounts.
bird:food_inspection_2: This database tracks municipal food-safety inspections of licensed food establishments such as restaurants, cafeterias, and culinary schools, recording each facility's location, risk level, and ward along with the outcome of every inspection. The only people in it are the health-department staff in the employee table—sanitarians, supervisors, and division managers, each reporting to a supervisor—who conduct the inspections. The main fact tables are inspection, which logs each visit an employee makes to an establishment (including follow-up links to earlier inspections and results like Pass, Fail, or Out of Business), and violation, which records the specific inspection points cited during each inspection, the fine assessed (Minor $100, Serious $250, Critical $500), and the inspector's comments.
bird:legislator: This database is a directory of United States members of Congress, tracking both currently serving and past legislators along with their terms of office. The people in it are senators and representatives of the U.S. Congress, stored in the current table for those now in office and the historical table for those who are no longer serving. The main fact tables, current-terms and historical-terms, record each legislator's terms of service, including chamber, state, district, party affiliation, and start and end dates, while social-media supplements the current legislators with their official Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube accounts.
bird:movie: This database is about movies and the actors who appear in them, storing details such as film budgets, box office gross, ratings, genres, and release dates alongside actor profiles including birthplace, gender, ethnicity, and net worth. The people in it are actors, held in the actor table. The main transactional table is characters, which records casting facts—linking each actor to each movie and capturing the character name, credit order, salary, and screen time.
bird:movies_4: This database is a film catalog modeled on movie data similar to The Movie Database, recording each film's details such as title, budget, revenue, release date, runtime, popularity, and voting statistics. The people in it are film industry figures stored in the person table, connected to movies through movie_cast, which captures actors and the characters they play, and movie_crew, which captures behind-the-scenes staff with their departments and jobs. The main fact tables are the movie table itself plus its junction tables—movie_genres, movie_keywords, movie_languages, movie_company, and production_country—which link each film to its genres, keywords, languages, production companies, and producing countries, with supporting lookup tables for reference data.
bird:olympics: This database is a history of the modern Olympic Games, covering the editions of the games (year, season, and host city), the sports and events contested at them, the countries or regions represented by NOC codes, and the medals awarded. The people in it are Olympic athletes, stored in the person table with their name, gender, height, and weight, and linked to their region through person_region. The main fact tables are games_competitor, which records each athlete's participation in a particular edition of the games along with their age at the time, and competitor_event, which records which athlete entered which event and what medal, if any, they won there.
bird:professional_basketball: This is a historical professional basketball database covering the NBA and ABA leagues, tracking teams season by season along with their wins, losses, scoring, and playoff participation. The people in it are basketball players, stored primarily in players and referenced through their IDs in draft, player_allstar, players_teams, and awards_players, and coaches, stored in coaches and honored in awards_coaches. The main fact tables are players_teams, which records each player's season-by-season statistics for a given team including playoff performance; coaches, which records each coach's win-loss record with a team in a given year; series_post, which records the outcomes of playoff series between teams; and player_allstar and the awards tables, which capture all-star game statistics and end-of-season honors.
bird:regional_sales: This database models the sales operations of a retail business, capturing who buys, what is bought, where, and through which selling group. The people involved are the customers in the Customers table and the sellers represented by the Sales Team table, which groups the company's sales staff by region. The main transactional table is Sales Orders, which records each individual order with its channel (in-store, online, distributor, or wholesale), warehouse, key dates from procurement through delivery, quantity, discount, and unit price and cost, all linked to a specific customer, product, store location, and sales team, while supporting tables like Regions and Store Locations provide geographic and demographic context for each store.
bird:retail_complains: This database tracks consumer complaints lodged through a company's call center, covering the calls themselves, the detailed complaint records about products and issues, and the company's responses. The people in it are customers/consumers, stored in the client table with their names, birth dates, contact details, and addresses, while the state and district tables provide geographic reference data. The main transactional tables are callcenterlogs, which records each complaint call with its priority, type, outcome, and server handling times, and events, which captures the substance of each complaint (product, issue, narrative, submission channel) along with the company's response, its timeliness, and whether the consumer disputed it; the reviews table additionally logs daily product star ratings by district.
bird:shipping: This database models a trucking or freight delivery operation, tracking shipments of goods by weight from customers to destination cities. The people in it are business customers (manufacturers and wholesalers, stored in the customer table, with revenue and contact details) and the drivers who transport the goods (stored in the driver table with names, addresses, and phone numbers). The main transactional table is shipment, where each row records a single delivery — its weight, date, the customer it belongs to, the truck and driver used, and the destination city — while supporting dimension tables describe the trucks (make and model year) and cities (name, state, population, area).
bird:student_loan: This database tracks students and their personal circumstances, such as whether they are disabled, male, unemployed, have filed for bankruptcy, have tuition payments due, or have had prolonged absences from school. The people in it are students, all identified by name in the person table, with the various attribute tables (disabled, unemployed, male, and so on) qualifying those same students. The main transactional tables are enlist, which records which organization a student enlisted in, and enrolled, which records the school each student attends along with the month of enrollment.
bird:synthea: This database is a synthetic electronic health record system that documents the medical history of a patient population. The only people in it are the patients themselves, whose demographic and identity details (name, birth and death dates, SSN, address, race, gender, and so on) are held in the patients table. The main transactional tables record clinical events anchored on visits: encounters captures each medical encounter, while allergies, careplans, conditions, immunizations, medications, observations, procedures, and claims record the diagnoses, treatments, measurements, and billing tied to those encounters, with all_prevalences serving as reference data on how common each disease is in the living population.
bird:student_club: This database is an administrative system for a student club or organization, tracking its membership, the events it runs, and the money flowing in and out of the group. The people in the database are the club members, stored in the member table along with their contact details, club position, academic major, and hometown ZIP code, with major and zip_code serving as supporting reference tables. The main transactional tables are attendance, which records which members attended which events; budget and expense, which capture how much was allocated and spent for each spending category of each event; and income, which records funds received from sources such as dues or the annual university allocation.
bird:superhero: This database is a catalog of comic-book superheroes, capturing each character's identity, physical traits, and origin metadata. The people in it are the superheroes themselves, stored in the superhero table with their hero name, full name, gender, eye/hair/skin colour, race, publisher, moral alignment, height, and weight, each described via small lookup tables for alignment, colour, gender, publisher, race, attribute, and superpower. The main fact-like tables are the junction tables hero_attribute, which records a numeric rating of each hero on traits like strength or intelligence, and hero_power, which records which specific powers (such as flight) each hero possesses.
spider2:IPL: This is a cricket results database, most likely covering a Twenty20 league with multiple seasons, that captures matches between teams down to the individual delivery. The people in it are cricketers, held in the player table, which stores each player's name, date of birth, batting hand, bowling style, and country, with player_match linking them to the matches they played and their role for each team. The main fact tables record the on-field action: match holds the fixture-level facts such as teams, venue, toss, result, and man of the match, while ball_by_ball records every delivery bowled, and batsman_scored, wicket_taken, and extra_runs record the runs, dismissals, and extras arising from each ball.
spider2:WWE: This database catalogs professional wrestling, tracking matches across promotions, events, venues, and championship belts, and it appears to have been assembled by scraping web pages, given the raw HTML and URL columns in Tables and Cards. The only people recorded are the wrestlers themselves, stored in the Wrestlers table and referenced as winners and losers in Matches. The main transactional tables are Cards, which represent an event card held at a location on a date under a given promotion, and Matches, which record each individual bout's winner, loser, win type, match type, duration, and whether a title changed hands.
spider2:school_scheduling: This is a university course scheduling and academic records database, tracking the physical campus (buildings and classrooms), the curriculum (subjects, categories, majors, and departments), and the scheduled offerings of courses with their times, days, credit values, and room assignments. The people in it are the Students, the general Staff, and the Faculty, with Faculty being a specialization of Staff identified by shared staff IDs, and one staff member serving as each department's chair. The main transactional tables are Classes, which record individual course sections and when and where they meet, plus the association tables Student_Schedules, Faculty_Classes, Faculty_Subjects, and Faculty_Categories, which record enrollments and grades, teaching assignments, subject proficiencies, and teaching categories, respectively.
spider1:college_2: This is a university database that models the academic operations of a college, covering departments, courses and their prerequisites, classroom buildings and rooms, and weekly time slots. The people in it are instructors and students, each attached to a department (instructors have salaries, students accumulate credit totals), and an advisor relationship links each student to a supervising instructor. The main transactional tables record semester-by-semester teaching and enrollment: section captures each offering of a course in a particular semester, year, classroom, and time slot, teaches links an instructor to the section he or she leads, and takes records each student's enrollment in a section along with the grade received.
spider1:hr_1: This is a human resources database for tracking an organization's workforce structure, covering geographic regions, countries, office locations, departments, job types, and staff. The only people in it are the employees, whose personal and employment details—names, contact information, hire dates, salaries, commissions, managers, and departments—are recorded alongside the jobs they hold. The main transactional or fact data is the job history, which logs each employee's past assignments, capturing the job and department they worked in over a given start-to-end date range.
